findings.old_behavior: H2HeaderStrictness directive was available to control HTTP/2 header strictness level (rfc7540, rfc9113, or highest). Configs using this directive were valid and accepted by httpd.
findings.new_behavior: The H2HeaderStrictness directive and its handler function h2_conf_set_header_strictness are completely removed. Any httpd configuration that uses this directive will cause a startup failure with an 'unknown directive' error.
findings.compatibility_reason: Existing httpd configurations that use H2HeaderStrictness will fail to start after the update. This is a hard compatibility break for any deployment that configured this directive (server config or virtual host).

evidence.snippet:
AP_INIT_TAKE1("H2HeaderStrictness", h2_conf_set_header_strictness, NULL,
                  RSRC_CONF, "set strictness of header value checks"),

findings.why_not_internal_only: H2HeaderStrictness was a documented public configuration directive exposed via AP_INIT_TAKE1 in the Apache command table, usable in server config and virtual host contexts. It was user-facing with described semantics.
findings.uncertainty: None - the directive and its handler are completely deleted, and any reference to it in configuration files will cause httpd to abort startup.
findings.recommended_review: Confirm that the intent is to permanently remove this directive rather than deprecate it. Users will need migration guidance if they relied on this directive for security or RFC compliance.
findings.test_recommendation: Verify httpd fails to start with old configurations containing H2HeaderStrictness. Document the appropriate upgrade path.

findings.affected_surface: Public header API in h2_util.h - response header ignore function renamed
findings.old_behavior: h2_util_ignore_header(const char *name) returned true for connection, proxy-connection, upgrade, keep-alive, and transfer-encoding headers. It was declared in the public header h2_util.h and called from h2_c2_filter.c and h2_util.c.
findings.new_behavior: h2_util_ignore_header is removed from public header and implementation. It is functionally replaced by h2_util_ignore_resp_header(const char *name) which checks only upgrade, connection, keep-alive, and transfer-encoding (no longer checks proxy-connection). Internal callers are updated to use the new name.
findings.compatibility_reason: Any external code or third-party module that declares or calls h2_util_ignore_header will fail to link (undefined symbol). The replacement function has a different name and slightly different semantics (proxy-connection no longer filtered).
findings.why_not_internal_only: h2_util_ignore_header was a non-static function declared in a public header (h2_util.h) installed as part of the mod_http2 module. It was callable by other Apache modules and its removal breaks symbol linkage.
findings.uncertainty: The proxy-connection header check removal appears intentional since proxy-connection is in IgnoredRequestHeaders but not in IgnoredResponseHeaders. This is a deliberate design change.
findings.recommended_review: Verify no external Apache modules depend on h2_util_ignore_header outside the mod_http2 module itself. Confirm the proxy-connection exclusion from response headers is correct.
findings.test_recommendation: Verify that all internal callers are updated (h2_c2_filter.c, h2_util.c). Test that connection-related headers are correctly filtered in both request and response contexts.

findings.old_behavior: h2_res_ignore_trailer checked only the IgnoredResponseTrailers list (age, date, vary, cookie, expires, warning, location, retry-after, cache-control, www-authenticate, proxy-authenticate).

findings.recommended_review: Verify that the expanded filtering of response trailers (now including connection-related headers from IgnoredResponseHeaders) is intentional.
findings.test_recommendation: Test that response trailers matching upgrade, connection, keep-alive, transfer-encoding are correctly filtered.

findings.affected_surface: Public header macros in h2_util.h - nghttp2 helper macros removed
findings.old_behavior: Four macros were publicly available in h2_util.h: H2_HD_MATCH_LIT_CS (case-insensitive header name match), H2_CREATE_NV_LIT_CS, H2_CREATE_NV_CS_LIT, H2_CREATE_NV_CS_CS (nghttp2_nv struct creation helpers). These were meant for constructing nghttp2 name-value pairs with string literals.
findings.new_behavior: All four macros are removed from the public header. H2_HD_MATCH_LIT_CS usage is replaced by the contains_name() function using IgnoredResponseHeaders literal array internally.
findings.compatibility_reason: Any code that includes h2_util.h and uses any of these four macros will fail to compile. These macros were part of the public API surface and their removal is an ABI break for any code that depended on them.
findings.why_not_internal_only: These macros were defined in a public header included by other Apache modules, without any internal-only guard.
findings.uncertainty: These macros were likely intended as internal helpers for mod_http2 implementation details. If any external module used them, it will break at compile time.
findings.recommended_review: None - the macros are clearly removed as part of the code clean-up. The H2_HD_MATCH_LIT macro (without _CS suffix) is preserved.
findings.test_recommendation: Full compilation of the httpd tree without these macros. Verify mod_http2 compiles and operates correctly after their removal.

H2_CONF_COPY_FILES,

findings.affected_surface: HTTP/2 field value whitespace handling - nghttp2 validation always disabled, manual stripping added
findings.old_behavior: The nghttp2 library would optionally RST (reject) HTTP/2 streams containing field values with leading or trailing whitespace. The behavior was configurable via H2HeaderStrictness: rfc7540 value (< 9113) allowed it, while rfc9113 (>= 9113) caused stream rejection.
findings.new_behavior: The RFC 9113 whitespace validation in nghttp2 is always disabled (parameter always 1). Instead, mod_http2 itself strips whitespace from field values using strip_field_value_ws(). Whitespace in HTTP/2 field values is silently accepted and removed rather than causing stream rejection.
findings.compatibility_reason: This is a significant behavioral change: 1) Clients that previously received RST_STREAM for whitespace-containing headers will now succeed, and 2) Backend applications will see field values that differ from what the client sent (spaces/tabs stripped). Applications with exact header value comparisons may behave differently.
findings.why_not_internal_only: This changes the observable HTTP/2 protocol behavior visible to all HTTP/2 clients and backends. The field values received by Apache modules and applications will differ from the original client-sent values.
findings.uncertainty: Applications that rely on exact field value bytes (e.g., cryptographic signing of header values) could see modified inputs. The change aims to align HTTP/2 behavior with HTTP/1.1 but the switch from configurable to always-on is noteworthy.
findings.recommended_review: Consider whether preserving the ability to reject streams with whitespace (rather than silently stripping) is needed for security-critical deployments. Verify no HTTP/2 extension headers carry whitespace-sensitive values.
findings.test_recommendation: Test HTTP/2 requests/responses with leading/trailing whitespace in header field values. Match behavior between HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 for whitespace-containing headers. Verify the test suite (test_203_rfc9113.py) covers all whitespace scenarios.

findings.affected_surface: h2_req_add_header function - input header value whitespace now stripped

affected_api.name: h2_req_add_header
affected_api.signature_old: apr_status_t h2_req_add_header(apr_table_t *headers, apr_pool_t *pool, const char *name, size_t nlen, const char *value, size_t vlen, size_t max_field_len, int *pwas_added)

findings.old_behavior: h2_req_add_header processed header names and values directly without whitespace stripping. The old implementation directly used the name/len/value/vlen parameters to perform ignore checks and table insertion.
findings.new_behavior: h2_req_add_header now delegates to a static req_add_header() which calls strip_field_value_ws(nv) before processing. Leading and trailing whitespace in header values is silently stripped during HTTP/2 to HTTP/1.1 header conversion for all requests.
findings.compatibility_reason: Header values with leading/trailing whitespace will be silently stripped. Backend applications (PHP, CGI, proxy) will receive modified header values. Code that compares or validates exact header bytes may fail. The public signature is unchanged but the input contract has changed: whitespace-padded values are now accepted where previously they would be passed through verbatim.
findings.why_not_internal_only: h2_req_add_header is declared in the public header h2_util.h and is the standard way HTTP/2 request headers are added to the request_rec headers table. Every HTTP/2 request passes through this code path.
findings.uncertainty: The whitespace stripping is consistent with HTTP/1.1 parser behavior (RFC 7230 Section 3.2.4). Practical impact should be minimal since HTTP/1.1 already strips whitespace. However, applications that receive headers via HTTP/2 with the expectation of exact byte fidelity may be affected.
findings.recommended_review: The change aligns HTTP/2 header handling with HTTP/1.1 behavior. The test suite (test_203_rfc9113.py) explicitly tests this new behavior.
findings.test_recommendation: Verify header value whitespace stripping via HTTP/2 using the new test_h2_203_02 parametrized test cases. Test with PHP, CGI, and proxy backends to confirm whitespace-stripped values are received.
